text: Course 13 made this point directly: the CTA credential isn't a multiple-choice exam you cram for. It's a live design defense in front of a panel of experienced assessors, and ServiceNow's own positioning requires substantial real-world implementation experience before anyone is even a reasonable fit for the assessment. This lesson isn't new information so much as making sure it's fully internalized before you plan your own next steps, because it's the single most common misconception new ServiceNow professionals have about their career trajectory.
There's no official, numbered sequence of years that guarantees readiness — ServiceNow doesn't publish one, and anyone who gives you an exact number is guessing.

What a realistic trajectory actually looks like is closer to this. First, an Administrator or Developer role from this path's earlier courses. Second — and this is the step people skip in their head — several years of real implementation work across multiple projects, with exposure to architecture decisions, integration design, security models, and governance tradeoffs, not just configuration. Third, one or more CIS specializations, earned through real project work. Only then does realistic CTA candidacy come into view. A developer who does years of competent but narrow scripting without ever being pulled into those broader conversations hasn't built the same readiness as someone who's been in the room for those decisions, even over a shorter span.

CIS specializations are a real checkpoint, not resume-building — they demonstrate you've moved from familiar with the platform to capable of leading a real implementation. If you finish this path and immediately attempt the CTA assessment, you'll walk in without having made real tradeoffs under real constraints. That's not an unfair bar. It's the entire point of positioning CTA as a destination credential — the panel is testing whether judgment built through real engagements is actually there.

Your honest next milestone after this course is a real job and real project experience, not another exam. Next up: weighing consulting against in-house ServiceNow careers — two legitimate paths toward building exactly that experience.
